props.title: True Grit
props.initialSlug: A fierce girl seeks justice with a gruff U.S. Marshal

sections.content: The Coen Brothers' True Grit masterfully reimagines the 1969 John Wayne classic, proving great Westerns still pack serious punch in modern cinema. Jeff Bridges inhabits Rooster Cogburn with weathered grit while Hailee Steinfeld's debut as Mattie Ross delivers fierce determination beyond her years. Unlike other recent Westerns like The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford (2007) that deconstruct the genre's myths, True Grit embraces classic Western traditions - revenge, justice, and the unforgiving frontier - while adding the Coens' signature dark humor and moral complexity.

sections.content: The film's success sparked renewed interest in classic Westerns, particularly character-driven narratives like Open Range (2003) and Appaloosa (2008). Roger Deakins' stark cinematography captures the harsh beauty of the frontier, while Carter Burwell's score draws from 19th century hymns to create an authentic period atmosphere. The film proves how the Western genre can still resonate when focusing on compelling characters over spectacle.

What sets True Grit apart is its focus on Mattie's coming-of-age story, joining other revisionist Westerns like Meek's Cutoff (2010) in examining frontier life through female perspectives. The film's formal language - from its period-accurate dialogue to its methodical pacing - creates an immersive historical world while maintaining modern sensibilities about violence and justice. sections.content: True Grit helped usher in a new wave of quality Westerns like The Hateful Eight (2015) and Bone Tomahawk (2015) that blend genre conventions with contemporary filmmaking techniques. The success proved audiences still crave well-crafted frontier stories, leading to innovative takes like The Power of the Dog (2021) and News of the World (2020) that explore previously untold perspectives of the American West.
